text: The customers who come back every fortnight pay the rent.
The margin on a box is small, which is why the number of boxes matters.
Turnover is what people brag about, and margin is what they take home.
Cake is perishable, so what is left at four o'clock is not stock.
I mark up from what the box costs me, not from what the next stall charges.
My neighbour David, who buys two boxes every time, has never asked the price.
The week that everything went wrong was the week the sun came out.
I made forty boxes, which was ten more than I had ever made.
A number you pick before you look is a guess wearing a suit.

I have had the same stall for nineteen years, and the thing nobody believes is that a good day means almost nothing. A good day is weather. What pays my rent is the forty or fifty people who come back every single week without being asked, and I could name most of them. A customer who buys because you are two pence cheaper is not a customer, because somebody else will be two pence cheaper than you next month. The traders who last are the ones who worked out early what each item actually costs them, and then stopped looking at the stall opposite.

The week I lost money was the week the sun came out, which sounds like it should be the other way round. I made forty boxes, which was ten more than I had ever made, because I thought a hot Saturday meant more people. I sold twenty-six. Cake does not keep, so the fourteen that were left were not stock, they were just gone. What I learnt was not to bake less. What I learnt was that I had picked the number before I had looked at anything, and that a number you pick before you look is a guess wearing a suit.

You add up what the ingredients and the boxes cost you. You add the overheads that you pay even in a week when you sell nothing. You count the turnover, which is everything that came in. You take the costs out of the turnover, and what is left is the margin. Only then do you know whether you broke even.
The customers who come back every fortnight pay the rent.
My neighbour David, who buys two boxes every time, has never asked the price.
The week that everything went wrong was the week the sun came out.
I made forty boxes, which was ten more than I had ever made.
The trader whose stall is next to mine undercut me in June.
Turnover, which is everything that comes in, is not the same as margin.
Turnover is what people brag about, and margin is what they take home.
Cake is perishable, so what is left at four o'clock is not stock.
A number you pick before you look is a guess wearing a suit.
